blocks.label: Directional Hypothesis
blocks.description: Predicts X increases or decreases Y (e.g., 'caffeine will improve test scores')

blocks.label: Non-Directional Hypothesis
blocks.description: Predicts a relationship between X and Y without specifying direction

blocks.label: Null Hypothesis
blocks.description: Predicts no significant relationship or effect between variables

blocks.label: Independent Variable
blocks.description: The variable you manipulate or control (the 'cause')

blocks.label: Dependent Variable
blocks.description: The variable you measure — what changes as a result (the 'effect')

blocks.label: Control Variable
blocks.description: Variables held constant to isolate the effect of the IV

blocks.label: Confounding Variable
blocks.description: An uncontrolled variable that may influence the results

blocks.label: Survey / Questionnaire
blocks.description: Collect self-reported data from a large group using standardised questions

blocks.label: Laboratory Experiment
blocks.description: Controlled experiment in a lab setting — high internal validity

blocks.label: Field Experiment
blocks.description: Experiment conducted in a natural environment — higher ecological validity

blocks.label: Observational Study
blocks.description: Observe and record behaviour without intervention

blocks.label: Case Study
blocks.description: In-depth investigation of a single individual, group, or event

blocks.label: Meta-Analysis
blocks.description: Statistical synthesis of results from multiple studies on the same topic

blocks.label: Small Sample (n < 30)
blocks.description: Fewer than 30 participants — limited statistical power

blocks.label: Medium Sample (n = 30–200)
blocks.description: 30 to 200 participants — adequate for most inferential tests

blocks.label: Large Sample (n > 200)
blocks.description: More than 200 participants — high statistical power, better generalisability

blocks.label: Random Sampling
blocks.description: Every member of the population has an equal chance of being selected

blocks.label: Stratified Sampling
blocks.description: Population divided into subgroups; samples drawn proportionally from each

blocks.label: Convenience Sampling
blocks.description: Participants selected because they are easily accessible — introduces bias

blocks.label: Snowball Sampling
blocks.description: Existing participants recruit future participants — useful for hard-to-reach groups

blocks.label: Likert Scale
blocks.description: Participants rate agreement on a numbered scale (e.g., 1–5 strongly agree)

blocks.label: Physical Measurement
blocks.description: Direct measurement of physical quantities (e.g., reaction time, weight, score)

blocks.label: Frequency / Count
blocks.description: Count occurrences of a behaviour or event (e.g., number of errors)

blocks.label: Interview
blocks.description: Structured or semi-structured verbal responses from participants

blocks.label: Open-Ended Questionnaire
blocks.description: Free-text responses that capture rich qualitative data

blocks.label: Observation Notes
blocks.description: Researcher records detailed field notes on observed behaviour

blocks.label: Mixed Methods Data
blocks.description: Combination of quantitative measurements and qualitative responses

blocks.label: t-Test
blocks.description: Compare means between two groups (e.g., experimental vs. control)

blocks.label: ANOVA
blocks.description: Compare means across three or more groups simultaneously

blocks.label: Chi-Square Test
blocks.description: Test relationships between categorical variables using frequency data

blocks.label: Regression Analysis
blocks.description: Model the relationship between a predictor and an outcome variable

blocks.label: Correlation Analysis
blocks.description: Measure the strength and direction of a linear relationship between two variables

blocks.label: Thematic Analysis
blocks.description: Identify patterns and themes across qualitative data (interviews, notes)

blocks.label: Content Analysis
blocks.description: Systematically categorise and quantify content in qualitative or mixed data

blocks.label: Hypothesis Supported
blocks.description: Results are consistent with the research hypothesis

blocks.label: Hypothesis Rejected
blocks.description: Results contradict the hypothesis — the null hypothesis is retained

blocks.label: Inconclusive Results
blocks.description: Results are mixed or insufficient to make a definitive claim

blocks.label: Further Research Needed
blocks.description: Findings suggest new questions — recommend future studies

blocks.label: Wet Lab Experiment
blocks.description: Controlled bench-top experiment using biological or chemical reagents in a lab

blocks.label: In Vitro Cell Assay
blocks.description: Test effects on cultured cells or tissues outside a living organism

blocks.label: In Vivo Animal Study
blocks.description: Test effects on living organisms under controlled conditions

blocks.label: Spectroscopy / Absorbance Reading
blocks.description: Measure light absorption or emission to quantify substance concentration

blocks.label: Microscopy Image Data
blocks.description: Capture cell or tissue images at microscopic resolution for morphological analysis

blocks.label: Sequencing Read Data
blocks.description: DNA/RNA sequence outputs from NGS, PCR, or Sanger sequencing

blocks.label: Survival Curve Analysis
blocks.description: Kaplan-Meier or Cox regression analysis of time-to-event data

blocks.label: Bioinformatics Pipeline
blocks.description: Automated computational analysis of genomic, proteomic, or metabolomic data

blocks.label: Ablation Study
blocks.description: Systematically remove model components to measure each one's contribution to performance

blocks.label: k-Fold Cross-Validation
blocks.description: Split dataset into k folds and rotate training/test splits to evaluate generalization

blocks.label: Benchmark Evaluation
blocks.description: Evaluate model on established standard datasets and compare against published baselines

blocks.label: Training / Validation Loss Curves
blocks.description: Track model loss and accuracy over training epochs to detect overfitting

blocks.label: Confusion Matrix / Classification Report
blocks.description: Count true/false positives and negatives per class; compute precision, recall, F1

blocks.label: Latency / Throughput Metrics
blocks.description: Measure inference speed, memory usage, and throughput at various batch sizes

blocks.label: Finite Element Analysis (FEA)
blocks.description: Simulate structural stress and deformation using a computational mesh model

blocks.label: Prototype Build & Test
blocks.description: Fabricate a physical or digital prototype and measure performance under real conditions

blocks.label: Sensor / Telemetry Data
blocks.description: Time-series readings from physical sensors (force, temperature, pressure, vibration)

blocks.label: Power / Efficiency Metrics
blocks.description: Measure energy consumption, thermal output, throughput, or yield ratio

blocks.label: Monte Carlo Simulation
blocks.description: Repeated random sampling to estimate probabilistic outcomes and uncertainty ranges

blocks.label: Failure Mode & Effect Analysis
blocks.description: Systematically identify potential failure modes, their causes, and downstream effects

blocks.label: Formal Mathematical Proof
blocks.description: Derive theorems step-by-step using axioms, lemmas, and logical deduction

blocks.label: Numerical Simulation
blocks.description: Approximate solutions to equations via iterative computational methods

blocks.label: Theorem / Counterexample Output
blocks.description: Formal mathematical claim with proof sketch, or a counterexample that disproves a conjecture

blocks.label: Numerical Approximation Output
blocks.description: Computed values from iterative algorithms with error bounds and convergence rate

blocks.label: Convergence Analysis
blocks.description: Prove or empirically measure whether an algorithm or series approaches a limit

blocks.label: Complexity / Big-O Analysis
blocks.description: Characterize the time or space complexity of an algorithm as input size grows

blocks.label: Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT)
blocks.description: Randomly assign participants to treatment and control arms for unbiased causal inference

blocks.label: Longitudinal Cohort Study
blocks.description: Follow the same participants over an extended time period to track changes

blocks.label: Focus Group
blocks.description: Moderated group discussion (6–10 participants) to explore shared attitudes and perceptions

blocks.label: Behavioral Coding Sheet
blocks.description: Trained coders categorize observed behaviors using a standardized coding scheme

blocks.label: Physiological Measure (EEG/fMRI/GSR)
blocks.description: Record brain activity, galvanic skin response, or heart rate during a controlled task

blocks.label: Structural Equation Modeling (SEM)
blocks.description: Model complex causal relationships among latent and observed variables simultaneously

blocks.label: Effect Size (Cohen's d / η²)
blocks.description: Quantify the practical magnitude of an observed difference beyond statistical significance
